newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa maize plantings almost completed.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa maize plantings almost completed.

text.p: South African maize plantings have almost been completed and indications were that no more maize than last season would be planted, the National Association of Maize Producers (Nampo) said on Thursday.

Nampo chairman Japie Grobler said cold and wet conditions in the Mpumalanga and Eastern Cape provinces resulted in a late start to plantings which could affect the 1997/1998 maize crop in the two areas.
"In the rest of the summer planting area, farmers could start planting at the normal time," Grobler said in a statement.
He said thunderstorms and strong winds caused considerable damage in the northwest Free State province and in the Northwest province and some farmers would have to replant some of their land.
"In general the crop prospects looks good at this stage," Grobler said, but added:
"The final crop yield would be determined by weather conditions and rainfall in January, February and March, 1997".
South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee puts this year's maize crop at 9.48 million tonnes, up from 4.41 million tonnes in the previous year.
